data.title: bn-3f4s: Fence verification admission and enforce run allowance
data.description: Fenced local verification admission pins the normalized input, expected lead revision, current engagement revision, exact manifest pointer and pass digest. The same SQLite transaction enforces max_verify_runs per engagement, with exact same-key replay retaining its receipt. A deferred adapter opener runs only after conflict ownership is claimed. Passive pass status supplies the native pass identity, with exact accepted path and digest. Focused local tests, strict all-feature workspace Clippy and the full serialized offline just check passed. Native target qualification was not invoked.

data.body: risk:high — The public metadata path can mint a verify key without enforcing the engagement allowance. `declare_request` passes `None` for pins, so it skips the count and refusal in lines 824–843. The same key is then admissible through normal verification preflight: the replay branches at lines 784–815 check the stored input and pins, but the store has no persisted distinction between a fenced acceptance and a metadata-only one. With a one-run allowance already consumed, an extra metadata-only verify acceptance can therefore become a Prepared run despite the cap. Guard all fresh verify acceptance paths, or persist and enforce eligibility before a legacy or metadata-only acceptance can become executable. Keep historical keys readable and counted. Add coverage that the public path cannot make a fresh over-cap verify key execution-eligible.

risk:medium — Exact-key replay loses the original receipt after an engagement amendment. The replay loads the persisted acceptance, then passes its historical engagement revision into `check_verification_pins`, which requires the supplied manifest revision and the database MAX revision to match that historical value (lines 2150–2166). After a declaration on revision 1 and amendment to revision 2, both supplying the original manifest and supplying current inputs fail to return the existing acceptance. Resolving and freezing inputs before stored-key lookup in `preflight::declare` also lets moved inputs fail with integrity or resolution errors before the stored replay is returned. Plan INV-13 and section 7.5 require the same run and receipt. Resolve scope and canonical input against the stored key first, return its persisted acceptance without another debit, and separately fence live resumption against current authority at conflict acquisition. Cover a retry after amendment at an exhausted cap and verify there is no revision, row, audit, or adapter activity from replay alone.

Failure-mode review. (1) A metadata-created key can bypass the cap, an amendment can hide a receipt, and pre-start failures consume a durable admission by design. (2) Cover concurrent distinct keys for the last slot, concurrent identical retries, foreign scopes, pre-existing rows, stops between declaration and claim, amendments on either side of claim, and mismatched native ID, digest or pass path. (3) Keep the patch unmerged until both findings are addressed. For any existing state, preserve SQLite keys, receipts, and audit history during rollback, and reconcile in-progress runs before re-enabling dispatch. (4) Use the existing request acceptance audit and typed refusal codes to monitor admitted count versus manifest allowance, repeat key/revision conflicts and adapter-open failures, with no pass path or identifier in diagnostic fields. (5) Compare scoped canonical input before mutable resolution on replay. For a fresh admission verify selected and expected lead revisions, the current engagement pointer with exact artifact/revision/manifest digest/pass digest, typed rounds, the budget, and the fresh gate-validated native pass file and digest before accounting.

data.reason: Fresh metadata-only verify keys can become executable beyond the admission allowance (th-fe3iys). Exact same-key declaration after an amendment loses the original receipt (th-1oujb1).

data.body: Fixed. A fresh fenced verification writes a distinct audit receipt in the same immediate transaction as the allowance check and key. Conflict claims and new step inserts require that exact typed receipt for verify keys. Metadata-only and historical keys remain readable and counted. Existing historical step outcomes can be reconciled without starting a new step. Regression tests exercise the public over-cap path, the last slot under concurrent distinct keys, concurrent identical keys and retained historical claims.

Fixed. Declaration looks up scoped canonical bytes and returns the original acceptance before rebuilding selectors or the experiment. A separate live conflict transaction validates the current stop and engagement head, exact manifest and pass pointers, and eligibility before opening adapters. The exhausted-cap amendment test reopens the same receipt with both old and amended inputs, then verifies that live preparation refuses with no adapter call or store writes.

risk:medium — A fresh metadata-only verify declaration can still persist step intents and outcomes. The declared/empty-step guard applies only when `pins.is_some()`, so the public `declare_request` can write every caller-bundled step via `create_run` (lines 3079–3098) before its metadata receipt exists. The new historical reconciliation test actually creates its purported historical intent through that fresh public API (store/request_tests.rs:273–289). Recovery then treats this row as a durable execution intent, including unresolved-dispatch status. Require fresh verify requests to be declared and empty on both acceptance paths. Load pre-fence steps from a historical database fixture and cover rejection of bundled steps without a receipt, audit advance, or run row.

risk:medium — A fresh metadata-only verify declaration can persist step intents and outcomes. The declared/empty-step guard applies only when `pins.is_some()`. `create_run` at lines 3079–3098 inserts caller-bundled steps before the metadata receipt exists. The historical reconciliation test at store/request_tests.rs:273–289 creates its purported historical intent through this fresh public path. A recovery read reports the resulting row as a durable intent, including unresolved-dispatch status. Require fresh verify requests to be declared and empty on both paths. Seed pre-fence steps from a historical database fixture and cover refusal of bundled steps without a new receipt, audit advance, or run row.

risk:medium — The retarget exposes the issuer of the fenced eligibility receipt as a public store API. `declare_verification` accepts caller-constructed pins and an arbitrary experiment digest. The store checks revisions and the count, then writes `request.verify.accept`. It skips `resolve_preflight` and `registered_execution_plan` (preflight.rs:523–559), including the compiled round ceiling. The general public conflict claim (store/mod.rs:913–915) and step write trust the receipt as sufficient eligibility, so a declaration that preflight would reject can acquire conflicts and durable step rows. This crosses the local admission boundary within the configured allowance. Keep the receipt writer internal to the validated declaration path, or require a sealed proof of that validation. Adjust synthetic publication fixtures without opening the production receipt writer.

The retarget closes the reported over-cap path into prepare. The exact typed audit receipt is checked before claim ownership, and the serialized allowance includes older and metadata-only receipts. I found two remaining local admission integrity issues and anchored them on the new target in th-2wlt2u and th-2mhak4.

Verified the amendment fix at 77095c0. Scoped canonical replay returns the original receipt before mutable resolution, and the immediate conflict transaction separately checks the engagement head and durable stop before adapters open. The separate bundled-step finding has its own current-target anchor in th-2wlt2u.

data.body: Fixed. Every fresh keyed declaration requires a declared run with zero bundled steps before creating any rows. Direct public API tests cover verify and another command with bundled steps or a non-declared state, and require no key, run or audit writes. The recovery test now loads step history from a pre-fence database fixture and proves that existing steps can reconcile while new ones are refused.

Fixed. The fenced receipt issuer is crate-private and requires an opaque declaration constructed only after preflight has validated the exact canonical experiment and registered execution plan. Publication, allowance and recovery fixtures exercise the validated public preflight entry. The compile-fail API test confirms the receipt issuer is private, and runtime tests reject an arbitrary experiment digest and an overflowing compiled request count with no receipt or execution eligibility.

risk:medium — A fresh metadata acceptance can still record unresolved dispatch without a durable execution intent. The declaration guard checks only Declared state and an empty step list. The run insert persists caller-provided effect and outcome fields at lines 3091–3096. ReadStore recovery passes the stored effects through to RunRecovery::has_unresolved_dispatch (store/read.rs:287–293), which treats Unknown as unresolved even with zero steps. Run show also exposes the stored effect through its normal projection. The public record_run compare-and-set at lines 705–724 can update the same outcome fields without checking execution eligibility or step history when the step list is empty. Require a pristine run on fresh keyed acceptance and guard later effect or outcome updates on metadata-only verifier receipts. Preserve reconciliation of existing durable historical steps and evidence. Add coverage that refusal leaves the key, run and audit untouched and that an accepted metadata-only run cannot later acquire an unsupported recovery outcome.

risk:medium — Recovery can report unresolved dispatch on a metadata-only verifier receipt with no durable execution intent. The fresh keyed guard requires Declared state and zero steps, while create_run persists caller-supplied effects, oracle result, reproduction and cleanup (store/mod.rs:3091–3096). RunRecovery::has_unresolved_dispatch treats stored Effect::Unknown alone as unresolved (store/read.rs:287–293), and run show renders the stored effect. The public record_run compare-and-set also accepts step-free outcome updates without the eligibility guard (store/mod.rs:705–724). Require pristine fields on fresh keyed declaration and require eligible execution history for later effect and outcome writes. Preserve reconciliation of already durable historical intents. Cover both fresh acceptance and later update, including truthful recovery and unchanged audit state on refusal.

Verified the bundled-step fix on b976c789. The shared guard rejects fresh bundled steps for every command, and the historical fixture seeds and reconciles a pre-fence step while refusing a new one. The related step-free recovery outcome finding is tracked on the current commit in th-1ctrbx.

data.body: Verified on b976c789. Store issuance is crate-private and consumes a preflight-owned declaration proof with private fields. Proof construction follows canonical experiment freeze, digest and engagement checks, and shared registered-plan validation. Store rechecks exact pins and serializes allowance with the typed receipt. Metadata verify receipts remain ineligible for conflict acquisition and new step rows. The existing exact-workspace logs cover compile-fail API privacy, invalid experiment and plan rejection, concurrency, trusted planning, and publication recovery.

th-1ctrbx: Metadata-only verification can persist an unsupported outcome and report unresolved dispatch without any durable execution intent.

data.body: Fixed. Fresh keyed declarations require pristine state, including effects None and no oracle, reproduction, cleanup, flags or steps. Public run compare-and-set cannot introduce execution outcomes before a durable step, and a legitimate no-effect pre-start refusal can still close the declaration. For existing durable steps, the summary accepts only supported effects, preserves stored oracle and reproduction until the typed publication transaction, and keeps existing cleanup authority. Historical steps remain readable and reconcilable. Regressions verify that rejected declaration and update attempts leave run, receipt and audit rows unchanged, and that both recovery and run detail still report no dispatch for unchanged step-free rows.

Verified at 70378f9 that fresh declarations require pristine outcomes and flags for every command, and that record_run refuses unsupported step-free updates. A genuine no-effect pre-start refusal remains available and an existing unkeyed row cannot be adopted. The fourth review found two separate paths that can still attach unsupported authority to those keyed metadata receipts, anchored on this target.

risk:medium. The public cleanup writer can persist a cleanup obligation on a step-free metadata receipt. It checks run existence and calls cleanup_bound_to_step, which accepts a missing cleanup step at 2731–2734. The schema permits owed objects without a durable step, and the writer stores the object, derives Cleanup::Unknown, and advances the audit even though this metadata receipt cannot claim conflicts or add steps. Keyed recovery loads that cleanup value and run show exposes it (store/read.rs:333, 807–815, 921–930). It also prevents an otherwise valid pre-start refusal because that transition requires a pristine durable outcome. Require appropriate keyed execution authority before creating a cleanup object, and bind later updates to durable plant or cleanup authority. Preserve the eligible pre-dispatch obligation and already durable historical reconciliation. Add a regression covering refusal and unchanged run, cleanup rows, and audit.

risk:medium. The public publication path with no acquisition also accepts a keyed run finalized before dispatch. The fallback asks only for a finalized run in the engagement and canonical record identity, digest and lead revision (1954–1989). It can stage a verdict for a metadata receipt with no durable steps, then complete_publication can link it into the verification index and advance the engagement checkpoint (1445, 1479–1504). Require the acquired-settlement path to stage a fresh publication for a keyed verification run. Preserve existing-intent reconciliation and the legacy path for eligible unkeyed records. Cover a finalized pre-start metadata receipt and require publication refusal with the checkpoint and audit unchanged.

data.reason: Keyed metadata receipts can still acquire unsupported cleanup obligations and publish a verification without acquired execution. See th-34anon and th-3dk0rr.

data.body: Fixed. A new keyed cleanup record requires a fenced verification receipt and exact conflict ownership. An owned Pending/Owed reservation may precede the plant intent. Ownership transitions require the correctly numbered, digest-bound durable plant and its supporting outcome, with existing historical cleanup still recoverable from durable step authority. The mutation matrix refuses Pending, Unknown, Established and NotCreated writes on both pristine and pre-start-finalized metadata without changing recovery state or audit.

Fixed. Fresh keyed publication must use acquired settlement and the exact fenced acceptance. Pending keyed staging replay, completion and reconciliation require the durable settlement receipt before any link, supersession or Investigation access. An unsupported pending candidate seeded from old state remains readable but cannot resume or advance the checkpoint. Finalized unkeyed records retain their explicit compatibility path. The mutation matrix also covers claims, direct and bundled steps, outcomes, experiment links and original links.

risk:medium. Previously staged and genuinely acquired keyed publications cannot recover after upgrade. The base writes request.accept for all keys (base store/mod.rs:765), then writes run.publication.settle and publication.intent atomically after validating the acquired run (base 1218–1263, 1778–1800). The target requires the new request.verify.accept even when an older pending intent has that genuine settlement, so both reconciliation and completion reject it before linking the checkpoint. Current positive fixtures mint the new receipt and miss this interruption. Preserve exact already-settled legacy intents with their canonical accepted run, durable settlement receipt, stored steps and record lineage. Keep refusing pending metadata intents that have no settlement. Add a positive test starting from the predecessor’s persisted pending acquired state, paired with the current negative test.

risk:medium. The new public lock_declared returns after installing the durable exact conflict claim and before prepare_declared checks the pass or calls the accounting adapter at lines 673–685. The public store writers already accept that claim and fenced receipt as enough to link an experiment and create and resolve steps (store/mod.rs:1124–1129, 1288–1296, 2644–2646). The separate scourge-verify crate tests drive that exact public route without opening an adapter (record/tests.rs:241–282). This allows durable dispatch history and downstream settlement without any successful verifier admission. Keep the claim helper internal, and require a capability minted after the accepted pass and accounting checks for fresh verification execution writes. Preserve receipt replays and recovery of already durable historical steps. Exercise adapter refusal and ensure that the durable execution history remains unchanged.

risk:medium. Pending publication authority is checked by run, so an unrelated candidate can inherit a genuine earlier settlement. The preceding target could stage through the public fallback after a prior intent was superseded, because that fallback required only a finalized run and the live-intent query excludes superseded rows. On this target any run.publication.settle after acceptance satisfies lines 1999–2004. The pending completion check at lines 1470–1480 then verifies record identity and experiment but never compares the candidate verdict, accepted revisions, effects or lineage with the settled acquisition. The same run-only guard permits reconciliation to access Investigation. Bind authority to the exact intent and candidate as well as the settled acquisition. Cover a bad pending replacement on an already settled run and genuine head-move replacement. The current negative fixture has no settlement, so it does not exercise this path.

risk:medium. The duplicate request-key guard handles keyed acceptance followed by import, and misses import followed by keyed acceptance. record_run checks only existing request_keys at lines 713–719, so a new unkeyed import can first persist a caller-provided key. The later fresh acceptance calls create_run, which checks only run ID at lines 3339–3347. The runs schema allows the same request_key on two different IDs, so both recoverable run records can name one key while scoped lookup returns only the later run. The matrix at store/tests.rs:1512–1518 tests only the first ordering. Make the reservation and alias checks symmetric under the same immediate transaction and preserve readable historical imports. Add a reverse-order regression, including a previously linked import where applicable.

Verified at 98209755. All fresh keyed declarations require pristine metadata. The compare-and-set rejects step-free execution outcomes and only allows a truthful terminal refusal. The mutation matrix checks the receipt, recovery view and audit state in both Declared and Finalized refusal states.

Verified the original metadata-only cleanup path at 98209755. A new keyed cleanup row requires a fenced receipt and durable claim. The positive pre-plant Pending/Owed test then requires the numbered, digest-bound observed plant for Established ownership. The separate admission-before-claim-writes problem is tracked in th-3pasuj.

data.body: Fixed. Conflict acquisition and raw experiment, step and cleanup writers are internal. Preflight constructs the execution authority only after the pass check and successful adapter admission. The writer binds that authority to the accepted scoped run and held claim. Settlement accepts an opaque ExecutedRounds value. Public historical reconciliation requires already durable step or object records. A passive refusal leaves no experiment, steps or cleanup history.

Fixed. Both import and fresh acceptance check the existing run-key reservation under their immediate writer transactions. The reverse-order witness links an unkeyed import, attempts both fresh metadata and fenced acceptance with the same key and different RunId, and checks that the import, scoped lookup, checkpoint and audit are unchanged.

Fixed. New acquired staging writes a typed audit receipt for the exact intent. A predecessor candidate needs its exact staging event adjacent to the same run’s settlement. Both paths revalidate canonical candidate data against the accepted lead and engagement revisions, completed steps, settled outcome and exact artifact lineage before Evidence replay or checkpoint mutation. The predecessor snapshot recovers through a simulated Investigation failure. A head-move replacement succeeds through acquired staging, while a standalone pending candidate with matching acquisition data cannot borrow the superseded settlement.

risk:medium. A genuine pending publication can become permanently unrecoverable after monotonic cleanup reconciliation. Staging validates the then-current cleanup result and accepts a resolved acquisition with cleanup unknown or partial (2054–2065). The public cleanup recovery path can later resolve an already durable object and update runs.cleanup (1237–1281 and 3294–3341). The new pending guard requires both current cleanup summaries to equal the immutable historical candidate. After a valid cleanup advance it refuses the exact stage replay, reconciliation and completion. Live-intent uniqueness at 1489–1494 also prevents an acquired replacement. Bind authorization to the immutable settlement and candidate staged together. Keep later cleanup state available for closure and preserve the original verification record. Add a pending keyed replay test with a monotonic cleanup advance between staging and completion.

risk:medium. The historical recovery API loses its path to link retained originals after a crash between Investigation commit and Store enrichment. The prior public link methods only enriched a null original on an existing exact flow. They now require the post-admission execution writer, while prepare rejects a run that already has steps (preflight.rs:630–632). The public historical step and cleanup reconciliation methods cannot fill that gap because their transitions require equality of existing flows (2948–2958 and 3340). Add a constrained historical enrichment API backed by qualified recovery evidence. It should bind the existing durable step/object and exact flow identity, fill only missing original references, and refuse replacements, new flows or outcome changes. Cover recovery after interrupted original linking as well as refusal for metadata without durable flows.

risk:medium. The compatibility branch recovers initial predecessor intents but strands a genuine predecessor head-move replacement. At the pinned base, a superseded candidate can be rebuilt by the acquired publication loop (verify record.rs:771–823). The already-settled fast path at base store/mod.rs:1783–1787 writes no new run.publication.settle, so base lines 1261–1266 persist the replacement with only generic publication.intent. This target requires adjacent settlement for that operation and refuses the pending replacement before Investigation access or completion. The positive target replacement test uses the new typed receipt and the predecessor fixture seeds only adjacent events. Preserve fail-closed behavior for the ambiguous generic receipt. If supporting its recovery, route it through qualified verifier readback and re-evaluation against the run's exact retained originals, and require verified completion authority before Store can link it. Add a genuine predecessor replacement fixture alongside the unrelated candidate refusal.

data.body: Fixed. Publication replay and completion use the exact immutable staged record and ordered lineage under the intent-specific settlement audit. Cleanup closure can advance independently. The regression stages with Unknown cleanup, advances it through public reconciliation, reopens the Store, then replays and links the original bytes while retaining the current NotRequired closure.

Fixed. Store recovery qualifies the exact persisted experiment in the Investigation case and reads the finalized capture for the exact Scourge run. It requires the frozen step and attachment key, exact verified artifact digest, decoded flow ID and completeness, and the bound cleanup projection. One transaction only fills missing original references, and repeating the exact attach is a no-op. The qualified local Investigation test exercises a historical crash gap, wrong selectors, and idempotent enrichment.

Fixed. A generic legacy head rebuild can enter verifier recovery only when an earlier superseded atomic settlement authenticates its entire staged snapshot and ordered inputs. Only generated record identity and the canonical checkpoint can differ. The verifier checks retained originals and re-evaluates the candidate, and completion checks concrete same-key Investigation receipts and exact lineage. A qualified local Investigation regression rebuilds after a genuine head move and links once.

Fixed for predecessor rebuilds. Ordinary Store completion refuses generic pending candidates. Recovery proves the same acquired staged snapshot and exact inputs against the earlier superseded intent and verifies the canonical successor checkpoint. The regression rejects an unrelated generic candidate even when its run and acquired lineage fields match.

Superseding my prior reply. A qualified Investigation receipt can authenticate exact bytes and lineage but cannot establish registered oracle evaluation. Removed the alternate public legacy completion route. Ambiguous pre-release generic head rebuilds remain inspectable and pending; current atomic replacements and the original adjacent historical settlement recover through normal verification.

The normal settlement gate is now the only completion path. The compile-fail test proves the legacy completer is absent. The qualified local Investigation test supplies an exact generic replacement receipt and verifies that both Store completion and verifier reconciliation refuse it without a checkpoint or revision change.

risk:high. A real ExecutedRounds proves acquisition, but this public method accepts arbitrary caller-authored record bytes and inputs. settle_publication_run checks the accepted run, step flow identities, effects, cleanup and lineage references, but never evaluates the registered oracle or compares record.result, round verdicts, reasons, exposure, reproduction or accounting to verifier output (store/mod.rs:2010-2080, 2304-2333). A caller holding a legitimate execution can change a verdict, canonically encode it with a matching intent and inputs, and obtain an intent-specific acquired settlement. The public complete_publication then accepts an Artifact with the matching digest and caller-supplied ID; it does not verify an Investigation receipt, stored bytes, lineage or independent reevaluation (1586-1615). Thus this path can publish a fabricated verification result and advance the checkpoint even though evaluate_and_publish would reevaluate and reject it. The same reason for removing the legacy public completer applies to this current public path. Make settlement/completion require opaque verifier-owned evidence proving registered evaluation and exact Investigation readback, or move the authority boundary so only that verified path can mint and complete an intent. Add a public-API regression with genuine post-admission ExecutedRounds and a tampered result or reason, asserting no settlement, link or checkpoint change; also reject a fabricated or unverified artifact reference.

risk:high. The unkeyed compatibility path lets public callers publish a verification without any admission or execution at all. Store::record_run accepts a newly constructed unkeyed Finalized run (794-825, 2701-2704), and require_unkeyed_publication checks only that this run exists, is finalized, belongs to the engagement and does not alias a keyed request (2114-2125). stage_publication validates record identity but no execution or settlement; require_keyed_publication_settlement explicitly lets the unkeyed run through completion (2133-2135). The existing a_linked_unkeyed_import_reserves_its_request_key_against_fresh_acceptance test (store/tests.rs:1748-1765) already demonstrates creating such a run and immediately staging and completing a record using these public methods, without any historical provenance or execution. Therefore a caller can bypass both run allowance and post-pass/accounting authority by choosing a fresh unkeyed run. Separate read-only historical imports from permission to advance a live verification chain: fresh stage and pending completion must require genuine intent-specific settlement, while any necessary historical recovery needs authenticated pre-existing provenance. Add a public-API regression that attempts the shown fresh unkeyed sequence and asserts no staged intent, link, audit advance or head change.

data.reason: BLOCK at 436e64a90a3ee81be5097d032008a60608f06b19: th-1amwnb permits fresh unkeyed verdict publication without admission or settlement; th-1cezzw permits caller-authored verdicts and unverified artifacts to be settled and linked using a real acquisition. Both public paths can advance the verification checkpoint without verifier-owned proof.

data.body: Confirmed on exact target with cargo test --locked --offline -p scourge-core a_linked_unkeyed_import_reserves_its_request_key_against_fresh_acceptance -- --nocapture: 1 passed. The positive test explicitly records a new finalized run and stages and completes the publication without admission; it is evidence of the bypass, not a security assertion. No target traffic was sent.

Fixed. record_run now requires a pre-existing run row and preserves legacy oracle result and reproduction. Fresh requests use declaration. Standalone staging exists only in core unit fixtures, and migrated unkeyed pending rows have no live completion authority. The external API regression confirms a fresh unkeyed finalized run leaves the run, intent, audit revision, and checkpoint unchanged. CLI history fixtures restore explicit migrated snapshots in their test databases.

Fixed. The registered evaluator and publication implementation now share the core crate. The public verifier derives the candidate from sealed ExecutedRounds and retained inputs. Crate-private Store writes require the evaluator's values, and completion uses exact same-key Evidence receipt, bytes, ordered lineage, case and registered reevaluation before the checkpoint transaction. A new stage audit marker and private receipt namespace isolate writable recovery. Older pending intents remain inspectable and completed history stays read-only. Compile-fail tests cover the raw mutators, and the qualified local test exercises public publication and replay.

risk:high. The supposedly sealed ExecutedRounds does not prove that its actual execution was covered by the pass and accounting admission. Prepared exposes pub admission and LiveAdmission exposes pub accounting (preflight.rs:324-334, 420-427). A caller can obtain a legitimate Prepared, replace prepared.admission.accounting with any AccountingCapture returned by public Teapot::begin_accounting (including one with caller-constructed AccountingBinding and no preflight_registered), and call execute_live. Separately, execute_live takes an independent caller-supplied Teapot and never compares it to the Teapot retained inside the admitted accounting capture, so it can dispatch on engine B while finishing the counters and pass for engine A even without field mutation. Lines 710-745 accept that other capture and mint ExecutedRounds; evaluation takes its accounting record as authoritative and settlement checks neither the run/pass binding nor the engine that dispatched. The result can therefore advance the verified chain with accounting and a pass that did not cover its execution, defeating the required exact post-pass/accounting authority. Seal Prepared/LiveAdmission fields and bind execution to the same admitted Teapot instance and exact run, key, pass, project and engine; reject substitutions before the first durable execution write or target request. Add public-API regression tests for swapped captures, a capture without registered preflight, and a different execution Teapot, asserting no step, cleanup, publication or adapter dispatch.

risk:high. Prepared exposes its frozen experiment as a mutable public field after lock_inputs, pass checks and accounting admission. A caller can change the owner or other session in prepared.experiment.principals before execute_live. RegisteredOperations::resolve validates the new session spelling and manifest property, but its registry digest and request count are global recipe constants, not the admitted experiment or session list (operations.rs:220-265, 287-299). execute_live checks only those constants and the authorized run ID before dispatch (rounds.rs:662-699); it never re-freezes the experiment against the accepted digest before effectful writes. Thus it can dispatch with a session that was never pass-checked or locked and conflict with another live run. Later verifier digest rejection cannot undo those effects. Make admitted run, experiment, artifact and admission immutable to callers and recheck the exact frozen digest, compiled dispatch plan and bound sessions before writing any step or invoking Teapot. Add a public-API test attempting session/experiment substitution, with assertions that no dispatch, step, cleanup or audit write occurs. An external Rust cargo-check probe at this target successfully compiled assignments to both prepared.experiment and prepared.admission.accounting; no target traffic was sent.

data.reason: BLOCK at 41779c10ad747ce26507e5c31e823345f910872e: th-1qwmo4 permits swapping admitted accounting or executing through a different Teapot; th-26w3jn permits substituting the frozen experiment and unchecked sessions after admission. These public paths break the exact execution authority before dispatch.

data.body: Fixed at cb2a4750d75fd67b300c16e144a1d7214b23c75e.
